title: Mitigating the effects of omission errors on area and area change estimates
relevance: Addresses our headline defect - OMISSION - specifically as it propagates into area and area CHANGE estimates, and gives estimators that mitigate it rather than merely reporting it. Our model is a documented high-precision under-predictor missing 30-35% of reference forest, so every area figure we produce is omission-dominated, and the change series compounds it. This is the missing piece between the Search 9 accuracy machinery and a defensible change number; it should be read alongside Olofsson 2014 (ID 69) rather than instead of it.

title: Area change estimates from sampling with partial replacement
relevance: The canonical treatment of the design that resolves our precision problem: sampling with partial replacement keeps some sample units across both dates (permanent, giving precise CHANGE because shared bias cancels) while replacing others (temporary, giving unbiased LEVELS). Forest inventory settled this in the 1960s - permanent plots give the highest precision for change, temporary plots avoid treatment bias - and our Phase 3 design currently uses neither, sampling each year independently. Old but exactly on point, and it is the reference for arguing a paired or partially-replaced design over independent per-year samples.
